shortfalls.title: Fractional amounts enter the ledger as whole cents
A second process can erase an acknowledged expense
An unrelated JSON file is silently overwritten
Some created groups cannot be used through ordinary URLs
Saving through a symlink leaves the ledger target stale

choices.text: Group IDs and member names must contain a non-whitespace character.
Duplicate names in the creation list collapse to one member at the first occurrence
A duplicate group ID takes precedence over invalid members in the same request.
Group creation returns a JSON object containing the ID.
Route lookup ignores the query string and decodes one percent-encoded ID segment
Unsupported methods and extra path segments, including a trailing slash on a balance route, return 404.
POST bodies are parsed as JSON regardless of the Content-Type.
Individual totals and shares use the JavaScript safe-integer range
Aggregate balances and transfers are emitted as exact JSON numbers even above the safe-integer range.
Balance and settlement responses that contain amounts require a Node runtime with `JSON.rawJSON`.
A missing data file is created on the first successful write.
A failed save returns 500 and leaves balances and expense numbering unchanged
Writes replace the ledger with an owner-only file.
The service listens on the wildcard address
`PORT=0` asks the OS to select a port
